subject: ALX status: scaling looks right, checkpoint restore is the risk
body:
Hi Priya, Bruno,

Status. Scaling behaves as advertised — going 32 to 128 TPU cores gives near-linear throughput on the ALS sweeps, and Recall@20 on the test split lands within 0.4% of the incumbent factorization job at roughly a fifth of the wall-clock. Recall@50 is slightly better than incumbent.

Risk: checkpoint restore. We save ALSState after every epoch, but restoring into a different core count silently reshards wrong and the next epoch's metrics look fine while actually training on misaligned state. We caught it because Recall@50 was suspiciously stable. Linnea is adding a core-count assertion on restore. Anyone doing a scaling study should not resume across topologies until that lands.

Rafael
